Question B-006-005-005.

Why the correct answer is right: High SWR means reflected energy is travelling back and forth on the line. Each trip through a real line dissipates some power as heat, so the effective transmission-line loss increases.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Increased receive noise level": Receive noise mainly comes from external sources and receiver/system noise; high SWR in the transmitting feed line is not the main reason a receiver hears more noise.
- sourceIndex 2: "Increased transmission line radiation": Feed-line radiation is usually an imbalance or common-mode-current problem; standing waves can exist on a properly shielded coax without making it the main radiator.
- sourceIndex 3: "Increased common-mode current": Common-mode current is caused by imbalance and inadequate choking, not by SWR alone, so it is not the principal adverse effect being tested here.
